SpaceX just acquired Cursor — the AI code editor millions of developers rely on — for $60 billion.

Here are the numbers that matter: Cursor generates roughly $4 billion in annualized revenue, with $2.6 billion coming from enterprise customers. The deal, filed June 16 as an all-stock transaction, is expected to close in Q3 2026.

But the strategic play is bigger than revenue. A joint AI model trained on xAI's Colossus infrastructure — one of the largest private AI compute clusters in the world — will ship inside Cursor and power a new product called Grok Build. SpaceX gets a direct distribution channel into engineering teams globally. Cursor gets frontier-scale compute.

What this means for technical leadership: the code editor is no longer a neutral utility. It is becoming a vertically integrated AI platform tied to a specific model ecosystem and compute stack. The tool your developers use to write code will increasingly determine which AI capabilities they access and which infrastructure your organization depends on.

Five of six analysts covering the deal recommend buying. Nasdaq-100 inclusion is expected around July 7. The market is already pricing in a scenario more optimistic than Street consensus.
